title: Meine Geschichte: Teil 2
summary: Week 2 capstone — numbers, time, V2 word order, questions and es gibt, then extend your self-introduction with your daily routine

blocks.title: Rückblick: Woche 2
blocks.body: Woche 2 geschafft! You can now count from *null* to *hundert* (and beyond, one glued word), handle prices and phone numbers, tell the time — **halb sechs is 5:30, never 6:30!** — name the days and months, conjugate regular verbs in the present, obey the **V2** law wherever a sentence starts, ask **yes/no** and **W-questions**, and point at the world with **es gibt** and **dieser/diese/dieses**. That's numbers, time, and the engine that drives every German sentence.
blocks.callout: Zwei Wochen Deutsch — du bist schon mittendrin!

blocks.prompt: Which sentence has correct German word order?
blocks.explain: V2 never breaks: front *Heute*, and the verb *arbeite* still takes slot two, the subject *ich* right after.

blocks.prompt: Type the German for 5:45 (the everyday way).
blocks.hint: Quarter to six — already looking ahead to the next hour.
blocks.explain: Viertel vor sechs = 5:45, counting toward six, same logic as halb.

pairs.note: Flip verb and subject for a yes/no question.
Add a W-word up front instead — the verb still holds slot two.

blocks.scene: Lena and Jonas want to know what a normal day looks like for you.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.nl: Na, wie sieht dein Tag aus?
lines.en: So, what does your day look like?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Ich arbeite von neun bis fünf.
lines.en: I work from nine to five.

lines.speaker: Jonas
lines.en: And in the evenings? Are you off work?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Ja, abends lerne ich Deutsch oder ich koche.
lines.en: Yes, in the evenings I study German or I cook.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.nl: Um wie viel Uhr isst du normalerweise?
lines.en: What time do you usually eat?

lines.speaker: Jonas
lines.en: Sounds good! And on the weekend?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Am Wochenende gibt es keinen Stress — nur Kaffee und Freunde.
lines.en: On the weekend there's no stress — just coffee and friends.
lines.spotlight: *keinen Stress* — kein flips to keinen for a masculine noun, just like einen after es gibt.

questions.q: What hours does the learner work?
What time do they usually eat?

blocks.title: Meine Geschichte — Teil 2: Mein Tag
blocks.prompt: Add your daily routine to your self-introduction — pick a time expression and keep the verb in second place.
blocks.sample: Morgens arbeite ich von neun bis fünf.

blocks.prompt: Meine Geschichte, Woche 2! Extend last week's self-introduction: your name, where you're from, that you're learning German — now add your daily routine with at least one time expression (Heute, Morgens, Abends, or a clock time) and keep the verb in second place. Zwei Wochen geschafft — weiter geht's!
